checks.3. Coverage: Covers WAL settings, page/commit protection, checkpoints/redo, insert/write/flush, recovery inspection, unlogged state and process-crash limits.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: The position-level mechanism is justified by diagnosis and recovery judgement; it stops before a WAL-record-format manual.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL crash/recovery mechanism. r18 gives general contract; r37 restore and r38 replication use it.

pieces.title: PostgreSQL base backups and point-in-time recovery

checks.1. Correctness: PG-A and current verifier: archive success follows matching persisted bytes plus directory sync; target uses actual exclusive XID 753, not scenario clock labels; reconciliation stays controlled and serial.
checks.2. Evidence: Fresh applicable verifier records base verification, missing segment 003 refusal, restored 3/3 before B203, source 30/2, raced fence refusal, first/repeat/conflicting payload and final 3/2. No concurrent general-purpose booking helper is promised.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers base/WAL dependencies, archive idempotence, isolated target, pause/acceptance, later valid booking, authority closure and controlled reopen.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: The complete worked restore is necessary operational depth; it does not claim remote/object-store durability from same-machine files.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL PITR procedure. r19 owns engine-neutral recovery judgement and r50 the Cockroach alternative.

pieces.title: PostgreSQL replication and a fenced promotion

checks.1. Correctness: PG-WAL/F: pg_last_wal_receive_lsn is received-and-synced progress, on can acknowledge before replay, remote_apply waits for visibility under a new snapshot, and lineage matters after promotion.
checks.2. Evidence: Native paused replay/SyncRep wait, local-only lost purchase, verified old-process fence and fresh-base read-only rejoin match the account. No pg_rewind or regional failure test is asserted.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers configured synchronous set, write/flush/replay, barriers, slots, lag, promotion, missing history, fence and rejoin.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Mechanism detail serves acknowledgement and failover decisions; platform HA orchestration remains outside the drill.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL physical replication/failover procedure; r20/r21 provide the general decision contracts.

pieces.title: Logical replication is a change contract

checks.1. Correctness: PG-LC and current native output: ordinary apply trigger behaviour, replica identity, publication filters/projection and PG18 missing-update/delete skipping differ from insert conflict stops.
checks.2. Evidence: Native identity refusal at publisher, schema repair, unsynchronised sequence collision, insert_exists repair and slot cleanup support the boundaries. Logical slot failover is documented, not claimed as a local experiment.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers initial copy/readiness, row identity, filtered transitions, DDL/sequence gaps, conflicts, resume identity, feedback/WAL and cutover ownership.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: The awkward omissions/conflicts are necessary to avoid treating logical replication as a whole-cluster copy. Broker/changefeed internals remain outside scope.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL logical replication. r38 owns physical history and r53 migration semantic acceptance.

pieces.title: PostgreSQL schema changes and their waiting rooms

checks.1. Correctness: PG-ALT/CI plus native locks: queued incompatible DDL can block later otherwise-compatible readers; validation and SET NOT NULL retain lock implications; invalid concurrent indexes remain a distinct state.
checks.2. Evidence: Current records include same versus changed filenode, blocking chain/timeout, skipped empty batch, invalid/ready index flags and waiting-writers phase. The existing index name is not accepted as proof of validity.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers lock/rewrite distinction, expand/bridge/backfill/validate, queue budgets, concurrent index phases, cleanup and deployment acceptance.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: PostgreSQL-specific locking/rewrite/index depth is justified. The general representation argument is not needlessly re-derived.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL DDL mechanics. r22 owns migration compatibility and r43 binary upgrades.

pieces.title: PostgreSQL sessions, pools and a blocked purchase

checks.1. Correctness: PG-I/X and native runtime trace: pool slots, backend lifetime, query cancellation and transaction ownership differ. PID is paired with backend_start; a failed transaction is rolled back before reuse.
checks.2. Evidence: Native two-slot incident records the 260 ms acquisition refusal, holder surviving cancel, failed waiter cleanup, still-blocked B, holder termination, B stock=0 and A retry changing zero. Pool availability ends at two.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers acquisition, active/waiting/idle states, blocker chains, cancel versus terminate, transaction cleanup, targeted identity and retry after capacity relief.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: The complete incident earns its detail by demonstrating ownership changes; no production library behaviour is inferred from the local harness.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL operation/session lifecycle; r23/r24 retain general admission/diagnosis.

pieces.title: PostgreSQL row security and privileged code

checks.1. Correctness: PG-R/SDF and current verifier: FORCE subjects the owner while superuser/BYPASSRLS remain exceptions; SECURITY DEFINER changes current_user, not session_user; pg_temp must be explicitly placed or avoided by qualification.
checks.2. Evidence: Actual login tests first use enabled/unforced RLS for unsafe scope=18 and shadow lookup=999, then limited qualified helper=20, including FORCE restored. Owner 0/super 4/bypass 4 and owner disabling policy are checked.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers spoofed scope, actual identity, grants, owner/BYPASS exceptions, definer authority, schema qualification/search path and transactional PUBLIC execute revocation.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: The detailed counterexamples are necessary to prevent a plausible but unsafe helper. Authentication/TLS deployment remains outside its local proof.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL RLS/privileged-function mechanisms. r25 supplies the general authority boundary.

pieces.title: Upgrade PostgreSQL with a real return boundary

checks.1. Correctness: PG-UP and native copy upgrade: file-mode semantics differ; checksum compatibility must be checked; starting the new link/swap copy can close a physical return path, and new business writes close an unreconciled logical return.
checks.2. Evidence: Actual 17.6→18.6 copy run records checksum mismatch/preflight, corrected fixture, preserved report, fenced old branch and new-only probe absent from quarantined old. Other transfer modes remain documentation, not runs.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers extension/driver compatibility, checksums, preflight, copy/link/clone/swap choice, statistics/instructions, cutover fence, validation and rollback/reconciliation.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Enough operational detail to choose and rehearse an upgrade; no universal speed/downtime or extension-compatibility promise.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL binary/version upgrade. r22/r40 own application representation and DDL changes.

pieces.title: CockroachDB keys, ranges and replicas

checks.1. Correctness: CR-REP and native 25.4 range output distinguish primary versus secondary key spans and column families. Leader leases normally co-locate leaseholder/Raft leader, with brief transfer qualification.
checks.2. Evidence: Single-node deliberate primary split changes primary ranges 1→2, preserves three rows and keeps the secondary span separate. It is not evidence of quorum failure, WAN routing or regional placement.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers key encoding/prefixes, hidden primary suffixes, families, range ownership, split/lease/Raft work and hot ranges versus hot rows.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Enough physical model to read later KV/placement evidence; no need to implement Raft or a range allocator.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns Cockroach physical/key-range architecture. r45 transactions, r47 execution and r48 placement build on it.

pieces.title: CockroachDB transactions and complete retries

checks.1. Correctness: CR-T and native 25.4 outcomes: replicated intents are not committed values; STAGING plus required in-flight writes can prove implicit commit; 40001 retry differs from 40003/transport ambiguity.
checks.2. Evidence: Native suffix-only retry leaves P3 wrongly at 12; whole retry leaves 10. Forced 40001 and withheld acknowledgement are labelled injections, and special restart-savepoint RELEASE is treated as committing.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers transaction records/intents, parallel commit/recovery, retry scope, request-before-stock, ambiguous resolution, savepoint API and multi-writer correctness.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Product mechanism and client contract receive enough depth without duplicating a complete consensus proof.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns Cockroach transaction/retry implementation; r13/r16/r27 own the general contracts.

pieces.title: CockroachDB follower and historical reads

checks.1. Correctness: CR-F and CR-T: closed timestamp plus applied/retained history support a historical read; bounded single-statement point-read/no-index-join restrictions and strong GLOBAL reads are separate modes.
checks.2. Evidence: Native Read Committed skew=0 versus Serializable retry=1, pre-purchase history, 25006 write refusal and bounded 0A000 are checked. Single node cannot establish follower routing, which is explicitly left unproved.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers chosen historical view, staleness bound, routing eligibility, transaction scope, writes forbidden in history, retention and verification at a real follower.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Enough API restriction detail to prevent unsupported substitutions; no invented latency comparison or follower-route proof.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns Cockroach historical/follower API. r28 owns distributed snapshot semantics and r48 GLOBAL locality trade-offs.

pieces.title: CockroachDB query work across SQL and KV

checks.1. Correctness: Native plan counters and CR key-range model distinguish SQL operators, KV reads/bytes/calls and distributed execution. DistSQL=false does not mean zero KV work; hashing does not remove single-row serialisation.
checks.2. Evidence: 60,000-row fixture gives 60 customer rows/15 qualified; routes read 120/20/10 KV rows with 2/2/1 calls and identical ordered IDs. Four hash buckets are observed on one host, not a throughput/balance proof.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers ordered/covering indexes, residual filters, KV locality/calls, join/distribution work, plan evidence, hash-sharding and hot-row limits.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Enough actual counters to compare routes rather than latency folklore; allocator/consensus tuning is outside the performance experiment.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns Cockroach execution/index performance. r44 architecture and r48 placement remain distinct.

pieces.title: CockroachDB regional tables and effective placement

checks.1. Correctness: CR-L/S and native 25.4 metadata support regional-table home, row-region gateway default and GLOBAL read/write trade-offs. Region-prefixed physical keys do not redefine tenant identity or global uniqueness.
checks.2. Evidence: Accepted policy is separated from convergence. Exact local record observes one shared range, five voters in 2 north/1 west/2 east and north lease; it explicitly cannot establish fully converged per-object placement or a region-loss test.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers gateway versus row home, identity/uniqueness, survival goal, requested/observed placement, global quota, write cost and locality verification.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Enough specificity for configuration/inspection judgement; candid convergence and licence limits avoid extrapolating a local capability into production entitlement.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns Cockroach locality implementation. r29 owns general regional reasoning; r49 operational movement.

pieces.title: Operate CockroachDB with the right identity and capacity

checks.1. Correctness: CR-R and CR-REP plus native secure operation: grants/RLS remain separate, runtime application labels are not identity, drain is not replica evacuation, and under-replication differs from unavailability.
checks.2. Evidence: Secure certificate/runtime tests include permitted and forbidden operations across populated shops. Local four→three-node decommission completes recorded replica movement; the next independent physical failure is not tested.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers secure node/client identities, runtime policy, capacity/health/replica signals, controlled drain/decommission, acceptance and failure headroom.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Enough operational boundary evidence without pretending that local process count establishes regional resilience or a complete production observability stack.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns Cockroach ongoing operation and node retirement. r48 placement, r50 restore and r52 upgrades retain their own acceptance boundaries.

pieces.title: Restore CockroachDB without discarding good bookings

checks.1. Correctness: CR-B/SB plus actual HLC-targeted restore: revision history must have been captured and retained; file inspection cannot replace restore, and the closed source history must be reconciled before reopening.
checks.2. Evidence: Full+incremental chain, missing-file check failure, pre-mistake 3/3 candidate, source fence race, controlled B203 first/repeat/conflict and final 3/2 are recorded. External effect is explicitly none.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers backup scope/chain, target HLC, verification/restore difference, isolated candidate, source closure, accepted later requests and authority acceptance.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: The worked end-to-end recovery earns its depth. Local licensed-feature execution does not claim entitlement or independent backup storage.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns Cockroach backup/restore procedure. r19 gives general recovery judgement and r37 the PostgreSQL comparison.

pieces.title: CockroachDB schema jobs and compatibility clocks

checks.1. Correctness: CR-DDL plus native 25.4 output: stored computed decimal is one write authority; DDL transaction limitations can leave partial schema outcomes. Failed unique job/index disappearance is distinct from completed GC.
checks.2. Evidence: Current SQL/result correspondence supports 50,000 rows, 133 overlapping updates, zero discrepancies, 23505 job failure and repaired semantic acceptance. Historical exact verifier identity is unavailable and is not promoted to an exact rerun.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers application compatibility versus job progress, backfill/resource limits, validation, failed job diagnosis, cleanup, uniqueness and semantic readiness.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Enough engine-specific job detail to operate safely. The 64 MiB failure/256 MiB success is a fixture condition, not a production sizing minimum.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns Cockroach schema-job mechanics. r22 owns representation compatibility; r52 binary/cluster version transitions.

pieces.title: Upgrade CockroachDB without finalising too early

checks.1. Correctness: CR-UP plus native 25.3.7→25.4.17 record: allowed predecessor, binary version and active cluster version are different checks; disabling auto-upgrade preserves the documented return window only before finalisation.
checks.2. Evidence: Record shows mixed binaries at cluster 25.3, an actual old-binary return with current history, all-new binaries still at 25.3, and explicit finalisation to 25.4. No post-finalisation old restart is attempted or claimed.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers licence capability versus entitlement, supported path, backups/health, mixed versions, rollback, delayed finalisation and acceptance.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: The two-version-clock detail is indispensable. No general claim about arbitrary downgrade or production failure tolerance follows from three local processes.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns Cockroach binary/cluster upgrade. r51 owns schema jobs, r49 normal node operation.

pieces.title: Migrate semantics, not just PostgreSQL rows

checks.1. Correctness: Native dual-engine comparison plus PG-I/CR-T: PostgreSQL wire compatibility does not imply integer division, integer width, constraint timing or transaction semantics. Immediate FK bridge is explicitly weaker than deferred enforcement.
checks.2. Evidence: Actual 5/2=2 versus 2.5, deferrable 42601, equal-count wrong-price detection, frozen copy, overlap, withheld acknowledgement and closed-history return all match. No network partition is inferred from reply withholding.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers semantic inventory, trusted-writer bridge, canonical value/report checks, copy/change ownership, target purchase, cutover fence and return reconciliation before PostgreSQL reopens.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: The complete acceptance/return path is needed for migration judgement. It avoids claiming a generic zero-downtime migration service.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL→Cockroach migration semantics/cutover. r43/r52 own in-product upgrades; r16 shared request outcome contract.

pieces.title: Distribute PostgreSQL with an explicit owner

checks.1. Correctness: CITUS and PG-FDW plus native evidence: co-location/distribution keys constrain uniqueness/references; foreign-server snapshots are independent; postgres_fdw does not provide remote prepared-transaction 2PC.
checks.2. Evidence: Observed same-server remote join/local Sort, two Foreign Scans and the mixed 20/19 result demonstrate pushdown and snapshot limits. Guarded movement tests runtime scope, epoch/inactive lock through commit and request-journal replay.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers local partitioning versus application routing/Citus/FDW, co-location, fan-out, distributed transactions, stale routing, movement fence, journal handoff and rollback.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Enough comparison and one operational movement protocol to make an ownership decision. Citus production behaviour remains documented rather than locally executed.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL distribution choices and movement handoff. r26–r30 supply general distributed contracts.

pieces.title: Full-text retrieval is a query and ranking policy

checks.1. Correctness: PG-FT and native vectors: configuration/stemming/positions, stop-word gaps, cross-field phrase positions and GIN’s lack of weight storage are accurate; rank scores are not probabilities.
checks.2. Evidence: Native fixture checks parsed lexemes, cross-field P9 phrase, query grammar, empty/negative cases and ranks 1.1/0.1. Large fixture has 200 lexical matches, 100 eligible before ranking/limit, then five results.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers corpus/field weighting, phrase scope, user syntax, empty queries, eligibility, index/recheck/rank work and relevance evaluation.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Enough retrieval mechanism to distinguish lexical matching from ranking quality without turning into a linguistics/search-engine survey.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL lexical retrieval. r56 owns vector/ANN retrieval and r33 general index choice.

pieces.title: Vector retrieval must keep its eligible set

checks.1. Correctness: PGV 0.8.7: filtered ANN can under-return and miss exact neighbours; strict distance order is not perfect recall. Exact filtering inside retrieval differs from limit-then-filter.
checks.2. Evidence: Current verifier binds 0.8.7, unchanged 30,000×8D fixture and one Repeatable Read snapshot, exact Seq Scan before indexes, one ANN index at a time and forced diagnostic paths. Independently recomputed overlaps are 0/20,20/20,4/20,10/20.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers chosen geometric example, embedding/model revision, eligibility, HNSW/IVFFlat budgets, iterative limits, exact baseline, cardinality versus recall, freshness and semantic evaluation.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: The comparison is deep enough to prevent a full page being mistaken for quality. Two-dimensional coordinates are explicitly non-semantic and no embedding model is feigned.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns PostgreSQL vector/ANN retrieval. r55 owns lexical retrieval; the common corpus/eligibility boundary connects them without duplicate full treatment.

pieces.title: Extensions add a deployment and integrity boundary

checks.1. Correctness: PG-C and POSTGIS plus native results: half-open finite nonempty ranges permit adjacency, exclusions protect overlap rather than capacity, and geometry distance uses SRID units; labelling a SRID is not transforming coordinates.
checks.2. Evidence: Native overlap 23P01, concurrent one-winner wait, GiST bounding-box candidate rejected by exact distance and same-host dump/restore match. Exact btree_gist/PostGIS/GEOS/PROJ versions and disabled network are recorded.
checks.3. Coverage: Covers extension trust/availability, version/library dependency, range shape, exclusions, spatial coarse/exact checks, restore rehearsal and dependency-aware removal.
checks.4. Depth, both ways: Enough two contrasting extensions to expose integrity and deployment risks. No extension-version upgrade, geographic metre conversion or aggregate capacity proof is implied.
checks.5. Ownership: Owns extension lifecycle and these range/spatial mechanisms. r03 constraints, r43 upgrades and r55/r56 retrieval link to it without taking over their subjects.
